delete.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Deletes a journal entry. Automatically-generated journals linked to a source record, and journals dated inside a closed financial period, cannot be deleted.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Journal id to delete.

message.description: Confirmation message including the deleted journal number.

400.description: Bad Request — the journal date falls within a closed financial period.

404.description: Not Found — missing journal, no delete permission, or an auto-generated journal that cannot be deleted.

message.description: Returned when the journal does not exist, the caller lacks delete permission, or the journal is an auto-generated entry that cannot be deleted.

500.description: Internal Server Error — the delete could not be completed.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Updates an existing journal entry and replaces its line items.

**Amounts.** Send the line amounts as `currency_debit` / `currency_credit`, in the journal's currency. The base-currency `debit` / `credit` fields are derived by the server (`currency_* x currency_rate`) and anything sent in them is overwritten - a payload that carries only `debit` / `credit` has every line discarded and is rejected with `400`.

**Line items are a full replacement.** The `JournalTransaction` array is the complete set: a line with `id` updates that line, a line without `id` is inserted, and any existing line missing from the array is deleted. A line `id` that belongs to a different journal is rejected with `400`.

**Balance.** The sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit`; `total_debit` and `total_credit` on the journal are recomputed from the lines and cannot be set directly.

The `{id}` in the URL identifies the journal. `Journal.id` in the body is optional, but when present it must match the URL id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Journal REF # to update

id.description: Journal REF #. Optional - the `{id}` in the URL is authoritative. If you do send it, it must equal the URL id, otherwise the request is rejected with `400`.

date.description: Journal date. Must fall inside an open financial period, otherwise the request is rejected. Omit to keep the current date.

currency_code.description: Currency of the entry. **Always send it** - every line item's `currency_code` is overwritten with this value, so omitting it blanks the currency on all lines.

manual_currency_rate.description: Explicit FX rate from `currency_code` to the site's base currency. Omit (or send `null`) to let the server resolve the rate for `date`. Do **not** send `0` or `""`.

alter_description.description: Overridden description, used for auto-generated journals. Ignored when it equals `description`.

number.description: Journal number. Auto-generated; send it only to override.

attachment.description: Comma-separated file ids to keep attached. **Omitting it detaches the journal's existing attachments**, so send the current ids when you do not intend to change them.

total_debit.description: **Read only** - recomputed from the line items on every save. Anything sent here is ignored.

total_credit.description: **Read only** - recomputed from the line items on every save. Anything sent here is ignored.

currency_debit.description: **Read only** - total debit in the journal's currency, recomputed from the line items.

currency_credit.description: **Read only** - total credit in the journal's currency, recomputed from the line items.

staff_id.description: **Read only on edit** - the creating staff is preserved.

entity_type.description: **Read only** - set only for auto-generated journals.

entity_id.description: **Read only** - set only for auto-generated journals.

is_automatic.description: **Read only** - `1` when the journal was generated from another transaction.

created.description: Time of creation for the journal

modified.description: Last time this journal was updated

JournalTransaction.description: The **complete** set of line items for this journal. This array replaces the existing set: a line carrying `id` is updated, a line without `id` is inserted, and **any existing line whose id is absent from the array is deleted**. At least two lines are required, and the sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit` (tolerance 0.001) or the request is rejected with `400`.

id.description: Existing journal transaction REF #. Send it to **update** that line; omit it to **insert** a new line. The id must belong to this journal - a line id from another journal is rejected with `400`.

journal_account_id.description: Journal Account REF # to post this line to. Get it from [GET Journal Accounts](/15115326e0). A line with no `journal_account_id` is discarded.

currency_debit.description: Debit amount **in the journal's currency**. This is the field the API reads for the debit side - not `debit`. Send `0` for a credit line.

currency_credit.description: Credit amount **in the journal's currency**. This is the field the API reads for the credit side - not `credit`. Send `0` for a debit line.

alter_description.description: Overridden description, used for auto-generated journals. Ignored when it equals `description`.

tax_id.description: Tax applied to this line. Get it from [GET Taxes](/15115346e0). When set, the server splits the amount and generates an additional tax line for you.

debit.description: Debit amount in the site's base currency. **Read only - derived as `currency_debit * currency_rate`.** Anything sent here is overwritten.

credit.description: Credit amount in the site's base currency. **Read only - derived as `currency_credit * currency_rate`.** Anything sent here is overwritten.

currency_code.description: Currency Code. Read only in practice - every line is forced to `Journal.currency_code`.

currency_rate.description: FX rate used for this line. **Read only** - resolved by the server from `Journal.date`, or from `Journal.manual_currency_rate` when supplied.

subkey.description: Transaction sub-key. **Read only** - set by the server for auto-generated lines (taxes, client/supplier postings).

journal_id.description: Journal REF #. **Read only** - taken from the journal being edited.

created.description: Time of creation for this transaction

modified.description: Last time this transaction was updated

get.description: Read operation. Retrieve all required pages before reporting complete totals. Returns a paginated list of journal entries. Results are ordered by date (newest first) by default and can be narrowed with the filter parameters below. Non-owner staff see only the journals they are permitted to view.

parameters.description: Number of items per page. Defaults to `20`, maximum `100`.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to return. Defaults to `1`.

post.description: MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Creates a manual journal entry. Send the `Journal` header fields and the `JournalTransaction[]` double-entry lines. The total debit of the lines must equal the total credit, and at least one line is required. Amounts are supplied per line via `currency_debit` / `currency_credit` (in the journal currency); the base-currency `debit`/`credit` and the journal totals are calculated automatically. The journal `date` must fall within an open financial period.

Journal.description: Journal header. All fields are optional.

date.description: Journal date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Defaults to today. Must fall within an open financial period.

currency_code.description: Currency code. Defaults to the currency of the transaction lines, otherwise the account default currency.

draft.description:
Journal status.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Issued |
| 1 | Draft |

manual_currency_rate.description: Manual conversion rate for a foreign-currency journal. Only applied when the account's "update journal entries currency rates" setting is enabled.

JournalTransaction.description: The double-entry transaction lines. At least one line is required and the sum of `currency_debit` must equal the sum of `currency_credit`.

journal_account_id.description: Journal account for this line. A line that carries an amount must reference an account.

currency_debit.description: Debit amount in the journal currency. Use `0` for a credit line.

currency_credit.description: Credit amount in the journal currency. Use `0` for a debit line.

tax_id.description: Optional tax id; when set, matching tax lines are generated automatically.

400.description: Bad Request — unbalanced entry, empty transactions, closed period, or other validation failure.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Create a journal category — a folder in the chart of accounts that groups other categories and posting accounts.

This endpoint creates **categories only**. To create a posting account that journal entries can be booked to, use *Add New Journal Account* instead; an `account_type` sent in this request is ignored.

**Required:** `code` and `name`.

`code` must be **numeric**, and it must not already be used by another category **or** by a journal account — codes are shared across both. Use *GET All Journal Cats* and *GET All Journal Accounts* to find a free code; by convention a child's code extends its parent's (a child of `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, …).

> **A code that is already in use does not return an error.** The request answers with `302` and a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page, and no JSON body — so check that the code is free before posting, and configure your client not to follow redirects for this call.

Omit `journal_cat_id` to create a top-level category, or set it to the reference of the parent category to nest this one beneath it.

Only the `JournalCat` object is read from the request body; any other top-level object is ignored. `Content-Type` must be `application/json`; another content type, or a body that is not valid JSON, returns `500`.

> **Do not send `id` when creating.** If it holds the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Use the *Edit Journal Cats* endpoint to change an existing category.

Requires the *Manage Journal Accounts* permission.

On success the endpoint responds with `202 Accepted` and the reference of the new category.

code.description: Code of the category. **Numeric only.** Must not already be used by another category or by a journal account. By convention a child's code extends its parent's — a child of category `5` is numbered `51`, `52`, and so on. A code that is already in use makes the request answer with `302` rather than a validation error.

name.description: Name of the category, as it appears in the chart of accounts.

type.description:
The normal balance side of the category — which side increases it. Defaults to `0` (Credit) when omitted, so set it explicitly: asset and expense categories are Debit, while liability, income and equity categories are Credit.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Credit |
| 1 | Debit |

journal_cat_id.description: Reference of the parent category. Omit, or send `-1`, to create a top-level category. Take the value from *GET All Journal Cats* — this is the parent's reference, not its `code`.

branch_id.description: Branch the category belongs to. Defaults to your current branch when omitted. Must reference an active branch, otherwise the category is rejected. Only relevant when branches are enabled for your account.

entity_type.description: Marks the category as one of the account tree's built-in categories. **Leave empty for a category you create yourself** — a category carrying this marker is treated as a system default and cannot be deleted. Values name the built-in groups of the chart of accounts (asset, liability, equity, income and expense groups, and the groups that hold treasuries, banks, stores, clients, suppliers, taxes and depreciation).

entity_id.description: Reference of the record identified by `entity_type`. Only meaningful when `entity_type` is also set.

disabled.description:
Whether the category is disabled.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Active (default) |
| 1 | Disabled |

id.description: Reference of the category. **Omit when creating.** If you send the reference of an existing category, that category is overwritten instead of a new one being created. Returned in the response as `id`.

parent_cat_ids.description: Comma-separated references of every ancestor category, ending with the immediate parent. Derived from `journal_cat_id`; any value sent is overwritten.

level.description: Depth of the category in the account tree. Recalculated automatically after the category is saved.

staff_id.description: Staff member associated with the category. Not populated when a category is created through the API.

total_debit.description: Accumulated debit total of the category. Maintained automatically from the journal entries posted beneath it; any value sent is ignored.

total_credit.description: Accumulated credit total of the category. Maintained automatically from the journal entries posted beneath it; any value sent is ignored.

is_recalculated.description: Whether the category's totals are up to date. Maintained automatically.

last_transaction_update.description: When the category's totals were last recalculated. Maintained automatically.

is_hidden.description:
Whether the category is hidden in the chart of accounts. Maintained automatically.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Visible |
| 1 | Hidden |

modified.description: When the category was last updated.

302.description: The `code` you sent is already used by another category or journal account. The response carries no body — only a `Location` header pointing at the chart-of-accounts page. Check the code is free before posting, and do not follow redirects for this call.

Location.description: The chart-of-accounts page the request was redirected to.

400.description: The category was rejected. Common causes are a missing or non-numeric `code`, a missing `name`, a suspended `branch_id`, or — on accounts that require every category to be assigned to a branch — a missing branch selection. `message` is `null` on this path; the detail is in `validation_errors`.

error_type.description: Error category. Empty unless the failure has a specific category.

extra_data.description: Additional context about the failure. Empty unless the failure supplies extra context.

validation_errors.description: Present only when at least one field-level error was produced, keyed by the field that failed.

code.description: `Required` when omitted, `Numbers Only` when not numeric.

group_id.description: Returned when your account requires each category to be assigned to a branch.

post.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Adds a cost center. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The request body is a flat JSON object. The account layer applies **no field validation** here, so the only hard requirements are the two fields the database cannot default: `cost_center_id` and `cost_center_ids`. Omitting either fails with a `400`.

In practice you should always send `name` and `code` as well — if omitted they are silently stored as an empty name and an empty/`0` code, which is rarely useful. `code` must be **unique** across the account; a duplicate `code` fails with a `400`.

`is_primary` marks a cost center as primary (root) or secondary (child):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Primary (root) |
| 0 | Secondary (child); defaults to `0` when omitted |

`cost_center_id` is the id of the parent cost center — send `0` for a primary/root cost center, or the parent's id for a child. `cost_center_ids` is the comma-separated ancestor path of parent ids; it **must be non-empty** (an empty string is rejected), and it is not maintained automatically, so the caller supplies it.

`branch_id`, `status`, `id`, `created` and `modified` are assigned by the server and are not settable through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <new id> }`. The message is localized to the caller's language (for example `Cost center Added Successfully` in English).

cost_center_id.description: Required. Id of the parent cost center. Send `0` for a primary/root cost center, or the parent's id for a child.

cost_center_ids.description: Required, must be non-empty. Comma-separated ancestor path of parent cost-center ids (an empty string is rejected).

name.description: Cost center name. Strongly recommended — stored as an empty string if omitted.

code.description: Cost center code. Strongly recommended and must be unique across the account (a duplicate is rejected); stored as `0`/empty if omitted.

is_primary.description:
Whether this is a primary (root) cost center. Defaults to `0` when omitted.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Primary (root) |
| 0 | Secondary (child) |

id.description: Id of the newly created cost center.

400.description: The cost center could not be saved — for example `cost_center_id` or `cost_center_ids` was missing, `cost_center_ids` was empty, or the `code` duplicates an existing one.

e.description: Error detail object (present for database-level failures).

error.description: Reason the record could not be saved — for example a required field (`cost_center_id` / `cost_center_ids`) was missing, `cost_center_ids` was empty, or the `code` already exists.

401.description: The Bearer token is missing, invalid, or expired.

put.description:
MUTATING operation. Verify target and authorized intent; reconcile outcome before retry. Edits an existing cost center. This is a v2 native-entity endpoint served from the `/v2/api/entity` base and authenticated with a Bearer token.

The request body is a flat JSON object and the update is **partial** — only the fields you include are changed; omitted fields keep their current values.

**The `id` in the request body is required and must match the id in the URL path.** It is what identifies the record to update: if the body `id` is omitted, the request is treated as a new-record create instead of an update (and typically fails on the unique `code` or a missing required field).

`code` must remain **unique** across the account. `is_primary` is:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | Primary (root) cost center |
| 0 | Secondary (child) cost center |

`cost_center_id` is the parent cost center id (`0` for a primary/root); `cost_center_ids` is the comma-separated ancestor path. `branch_id`, `status`, `created` and `modified` are managed by the server and are not settable through this endpoint.

On success the response is `{ "message": "...", "id": <id> }`. The message is localized to the caller's language (for example `Cost center Updated Successfully` in English).
